title: Local cohomology criterion for colimits of higher module direct images
statement:
Work in compatible universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites and let $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a morphism of sites presented by a continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $A,B$ be sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ respectively and let $\rho:B\to f_*A$ be a morphism of ring sheaves. For module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] use the direct image $(f_*N)(V)=N(u(V))$ with $B(V)$-action through $\rho_V:B(V)\to A(u(V))$. Assume module sheafification exists [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and both module categories have enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. Let $J$ be any small category, let $(N_j)_{j\in J}$ be a diagram of $A$-module sheaves, and let $(N,(c_j))$ be its colimit in module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix an integer $p\geq0$. Write $H^p(U,N)=R^p\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(U,-)(N)$ for right derived additive evaluation in $A$-module sheaves, and $R^pf_*$ for module right derived direct image, both computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Suppose there is a collection $\mathcal B\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal D)$ such that every object of $\mathcal D$ has a covering with all members in $\mathcal B$, and for every $V\in\mathcal B$ the canonical map of abelian groups
$$\varinjlim_{j\in J}H^p(u(V),N_j)\longrightarrow H^p(u(V),N)$$
induced by the $c_j$ is an isomorphism. Then the map
$$\varinjlim_{j\in J}R^pf_*N_j\longrightarrow R^pf_*N$$
induced by the same $c_j$ is an isomorphism of $B$-module sheaves. No filteredness of $J$, flatness of $\rho$, or closure of $\mathcal B$ under fibre products is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0H7B, lemma-higher-direct-image-colimit; module version of its sheafification argument using lemma-higher-direct-images (which is explicitly stated for ringed sites and modules).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-higher-image-cohomology-sheafification] with $q=p$. Write $P_j=P^p_{N_j}$ and $Q=P^p_N$. These are presheaves of $B$-modules, and the maps $c_j$ induce a cocone $P^p(c_j):P_j\to Q$. We have natural isomorphisms $\sigma_j:P_j^\#\cong R^pf_*N_j$ and $\sigma:Q^\#\cong R^pf_*N$. In particular the comparison concerns module cohomology throughout; no passage from injective module resolutions to injective abelian-sheaf resolutions is made.

source.place: Tag 0H7B, lemma-higher-direct-image-colimit, proof; module version using Tag 072W.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-modules-colimits-sectionwise], form $P=\operatorname{colim}_j P_j$ in presheaves of $B$-modules, with coprojections $\iota_j$. Its underlying abelian presheaf has $P(V)=\operatorname{colim}_jH^p(u(V),N_j)$, also for an empty or nonfiltered indexing category. The cocone in step 1 induces $\alpha:P\to Q$, uniquely characterized by $\alpha\iota_j=P^p(c_j)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Its component at $V$ is exactly the abelian-group comparison in the hypothesis, since both maps have components $H^p(u(V),c_j)$ on the colimit coprojections. Thus $\alpha_V$ is bijective whenever $V\in\mathcal B$.

source.place: Tag 0H7B, lemma-higher-direct-image-colimit, proof; module version using Tag 072W.

proof.text: For an arbitrary object $V$, choose a covering $\{V_a\to V\}$ by objects in $\mathcal B$. Every $t\in Q(V)$ has a preimage in $P(V_a)$ after restriction, since $\alpha_{V_a}$ is surjective. If $s,s'\in P(V)$ have the same image, their restrictions to every $V_a$ agree by injectivity of $\alpha_{V_a}$. These are precisely local surjectivity and local injectivity, so [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] makes the abelian sheafification of $\alpha$ invertible. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], with the ring presheaf already the sheaf $B$, this is the underlying abelian map of the module map $\alpha^\#:P^\#\to Q^\#$. Its inverse is $B$-linear: for a section $b$ and a section $y$ of $Q^\#$, injectivity of $\alpha^\#$ and its linearity give $(\alpha^\#)^{-1}(by)=b(\alpha^\#)^{-1}(y)$. The inverse is already a natural abelian-sheaf morphism. Hence $\alpha^\#$ is an isomorphism of $B$-module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0H7B, lemma-higher-direct-image-colimit, proof; module version using Tag 072W.

proof.text:
The universal factorization in [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] and the colimit property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] show directly that $(P^\#,(\iota_j^\#))$ is a colimit of $(P_j^\#)$: maps from $P^\#$ to a module sheaf $T$ correspond to presheaf-module maps $P\to T$, hence to compatible maps $P_j\to T$, hence uniquely to compatible module-sheaf maps $P_j^\#\to T$. Transport this cocone along the natural $\sigma_j$ of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-higher-image-cohomology-sheafification]. If $L=\operatorname{colim}_jR^pf_*N_j$ with legs $\lambda_j$, the resulting isomorphism $\theta:L\xrightarrow{\sim}P^\#$ satisfies $\theta\lambda_j=\iota_j^\#\sigma_j^{-1}$. Now
$$\sigma\alpha^\#\theta\lambda_j=\sigma(P^p(c_j))^\#\sigma_j^{-1}=R^pf_*(c_j),$$
where the last equality is precisely the helper's naturality equation. The colimit uniqueness therefore identifies $\sigma\alpha^\#\theta$ with the map in the conclusion. Every factor is invertible, so that canonical map is invertible. The argument only used coverings by $\mathcal B$, not closure of $\mathcal B$ under fibre products, filteredness of $J$, or flatness of $\rho$.
